requirement: Each requirement and example definition badge MUST link to its evidence detail page, and each rendered requirement and example MUST be followed by a "See evidence" link to that page. Each detail page MUST link back to the definition's anchored badge and, when an index exists, to the index. Reference badges MUST continue to link to the definition. These links MUST resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in `requirements.cli.mdbook`.
rationale:
**Verdict:** the sources satisfy `requirements.index.navigation`. The one marking gap is minor and noted below. **Implementation** - **Definition badges.** `replace_definitions` (src/lib.rs) renders each requirement and example badge as an `` that links to the detail page. This applies whenever a `DetailPlan` has a detail path for that name. Terms are excluded, which is correct because they have no detail pages. - **"See evidence" link.** The same function appends `

See evidence

` after each rendered requirement or example. - **Detail page links back.** `render_detail_page` (src/index.rs) emits `[View definition](#habeas--)`. That anchor matches the id given to the badge, via the shared `DefinitionKind::anchor`. When an index path exists, it also emits `[Requirements index]()`. - **Index entries.** `DetailPlan::populate` links each index row to its detail page with `chapter_href`. - **Reference badges.** `reference_badge` still links to the target definition with the same anchor. `replace_inline_references` and `replace_references` route through it. Detail pages go through `replace_references`, and `is_detail_path` and `detail_path` support that routing. - **Names containing `.md`.** `chapter_href` rewrites `.md` to `%2Emd` in every generated link: badge, See-evidence, index row, view-definition, index back-link and reference badge. This stops mdBook treating `.md` as a chapter suffix. - **Marking gap.** `reference_badge` and `replace_references` carry `{impl}` for `requirements.references.book_badges` but not for this requirement. Their link behavior is unchanged and goes through the `{impl}`-marked `chapter_href`, so I count this as a minor marking gap, not a missing implementation. **Tests** - `every_definition_gets_a_nested_detail_page_without_an_index` (src/lib.rs) covers: - Requirement and example badges. It asserts their `id` and `href` for names `zeta`, `alpha` and `cli.mdbook`. - The See-evidence paragraph, with exactly 3 occurrences. - The View-definition anchor, including the `%2Emd` form for `cli.mdbook`. - The case with no index, where the page has no "Requirements index" link. - `index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters` (src/index.rs) covers the case where an index exists: - Badge hrefs on the definition page. - Index rows linking to the detail pages. - The `[Requirements index](../../appendix/requirements-index.html)` back-link from a nested index location. - The View-definition anchor. - `links_preserve_requirement_names_containing_md` (src/lib.rs) tests `chapter_href` in both directions for `requirements.cli.mdbook`. It covers the detail link and the definition-anchor link. - Reference badge linking is covered by `references_in_nested_chapters_link_to_the_requirement_definition` and `fenced_references_render_their_badge_and_body_and_built_ins_are_unlinked`. Both are marked for `book_badges`. Neither uses a name containing `.md`. That case is covered only through the shared `chapter_href` unit test. Together these cover the boundaries that matter: index present or absent, requirement and example kinds, nested chapter paths, and `.md` in names.
